questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT

questions.stem: Maya's astronomy log asks which body fixes how electors are chosen.

options.text: Each state legislature sets the mode of appointment

options.misconception: assumes federal control over elector appointment

options.text: The national popular vote selects electors directly
options.misconception: confuses vote totals with appointment rules

options.text: The Supreme Court appoints electors by ruling
options.misconception: mistakes judicial review for appointment power

questions.explanation: Article II leaves the mode of appointing electors to each state legislature. Congress and courts do not appoint, and popular vote alone does not set the mode.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: Consent required for an agreement among states
questions.learningObjective: State when congressional consent is needed for an interstate compact

stimulus.body: Two states propose a compact to share water resources across their border. The compact would bind both legislatures for ten years. No federal agency is involved in drafting it.

questions.stem: Leo notes a water-sharing pact between two states and asks what consent is needed.

options.text: Only the two state governors must consent
options.misconception: confuses executive agreement with interstate compact

options.text: Congressional consent is required for the agreement
No consent is needed because states are sovereign
The President must ratify the compact
options.misconception: mistakes treaty ratification for compact consent

questions.explanation: The Compact Clause requires congressional consent for agreements among states. Governors alone or presidential ratification do not satisfy it, and states are not free to bind each other without consent.
questions.hint: The Compact Clause governs interstate agreements.

After each presidential election
After each decennial census
After state legislative requests

questions.topic: A line drawn by race and a line drawn by party

stimulus.body: A legislature draws districts to benefit one party. The plan does not use race as a factor. Challengers claim unconstitutional partisan bias.

questions.stem: Rosa asks whether the partisan map is clearly unconstitutional.

options.text: Partisan gerrymandering is always unconstitutional
Racial predominance triggers strict scrutiny
Courts defer to all legislative maps
Partisan maps lack a federal constitutional standard

questions.explanation: Partisan gerrymandering is not subject to a federal constitutional standard in federal courts. Racial predominance would trigger strict scrutiny.

questions.stem: Ken's log asks who fixes the mode of appointing electors.

questions.explanation: Article II leaves the appointment mode to state legislatures. Congress, popular vote, and courts do not fix it.

questions.stem: Two states make an agreement; how many congressional approvals needed?
questions.explanation: Congressional consent is required once for the compact. The two states must also agree, but only one federal approval is needed.
